findings.explanation: The new GET /users/<id>/export endpoint (export_user) fetches a user profile and all of that user's orders using the user-controlled user_id, but only enforces authentication via @require_auth. It never calls is_owner_or_admin(g.current_user, user_id), so any authenticated user can read another user's profile (including email) and their orders (status, total, shipping_address). This directly violates security-policy.md §2 ('A user may read or update ONLY their own profile... Use is_owner_or_admin(current_user, user_id) for this check') and §3 ('A user may view ONLY their own orders... MUST verify ownership with is_owner_or_admin(current_user, order.user_id)'). The sibling endpoints get_user (line 32) and update_user (line 45) in the same file correctly apply is_owner_or_admin, confirming the intended access rule that export_user omits.

evidence.content: A user may read or update ONLY their own profile (`/users/<id>`). Administrators may read or update any profile. Use `is_owner_or_admin(current_user, user_id)` for this check.
A user may view ONLY their own orders. Every endpoint that fetches an order by its identifier MUST verify ownership with `is_owner_or_admin(current_user, order.user_id)` before returning data.

findings.suggested_fix: Add an ownership check at the top of export_user, mirroring get_user: `if not is_owner_or_admin(g.current_user, user_id): return jsonify({"error": "forbidden"}), 403` before fetching the user and orders.
